zh.title: 阿聯酋航空工程部啟動 Material Futures Studio 學生計畫
zh.summary: 阿聯酋航空工程部啟動為期六週的 Material Futures Studio 計畫，邀請三所大學共 23 名學生參與，將退役航空材料重新構思為新產品。該計畫由內部 Upcycling 部門主導，與既有翻新及升級回收專案相連結。
body: 阿聯酋航空工程部啟動 Material Futures Studio，這是一項為期六週的計畫，挑戰大學生將退役航空材料重新構思並轉化為新產品。該計畫由阿聯酋航空工程部內的 Upcycling 部門主導，安排學生與航空專業人員合作，應對真實的產業挑戰。
首屆計畫共有 23 名學生參與，分別來自 Khalifa University、Emirates Aviation University 及 University of Sharjah。計畫開始時安排了導覽活動，學生參觀阿聯酋航空工程部設施，包括機隊的 A-check 與 C-check 維修作業，以及目前進行材料回收再利用的升級回收工坊。
在六週的課程中，學生將運用導覽所學，開發將航空材料升級回收並再利用為原創產品的新構想。阿聯酋航空工程部團隊成員將在構想與概念開發階段提供指導，計畫最後將舉行成果展示，由學生發表構想與原型。
Material Futures Studio 與阿聯酋航空更廣泛的翻新計畫相連結，該計畫是一項投資數十億美元、全面翻新 219 架空中巴士 A380 與波音 777 客機的專案，旨在提升機隊旅客體驗。翻新過程中拆卸的材料由阿聯酋航空工程部在杜拜以內部團隊進行升級回收，製成手工產品以減少浪費。
此學生計畫建立在阿聯酋航空既有的升級回收倡議之上，包括 Aircrafted by Emirates 限量版行李與配件系列，以及 Aircrafted KIDS 倡議。後者將翻新計畫中回收的布料與其他材料製成兒童背包，迄今已向 11 個國家的兒童捐贈超過 4,000 個背包。

en.title: Emirates Engineering launches Material Futures Studio for university students
en.summary: Emirates Engineering has launched Material Futures Studio, a six-week program pairing 23 students from three universities with aviation professionals to reimagine retired aircraft materials into new products. The initiative is led by the in-house Upcycling department and connects to Emirates' broader fleet retrofit effort.
body: Emirates Engineering has launched Material Futures Studio, a six-week program challenging university students to reimagine retired aircraft materials and turn them into new products. The initiative is led by the Upcycling department within Emirates Engineering and pairs students with aviation professionals to tackle real-world industry challenges.

The first edition brought together 23 students from Khalifa University, Emirates Aviation University, and the University of Sharjah. The program opened with an orientation and tour of Emirates Engineering's facilities, where students observed maintenance operations including A-checks and C-checks on the Emirates fleet, along with the upcycling shop where materials are currently being repurposed.

Over the course of six weeks, students will apply what they learned during the orientation to develop new concepts for upcycling and reusing aircraft materials into original products. Members of the Emirates Engineering team will provide guidance throughout the ideation and concept development stages, and the program will conclude with a final showcase where students present their concepts and prototypes.

Material Futures Studio connects to a broader retrofit program at Emirates, a multi-billion-dollar investment to fully refurbish 219 Airbus A380 and Boeing 777 aircraft aimed at improving the customer experience across its fleet. Materials removed from retrofitted aircraft are being repurposed through upcycling work led entirely in-house by Emirates Engineering in Dubai, with a dedicated team turning retired aircraft materials into handcrafted products meant to cut down on waste.

The student program builds on other upcycling initiatives already underway at the airline, including the Aircrafted by Emirates collection of limited-edition luggage, bags, and accessories made from reclaimed aircraft interiors. It also complements the Aircrafted KIDS initiative, which has produced more than 4,000 backpacks donated to children across 11 countries.
